This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 18-04-2024 at about 1-50 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in a Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LQ-0743 on Pipe line road and when he reached near B.F.W. Junction, Yeshwanthapura, Bangalore, at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-NA-8989 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioner, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Ramaiah Hospital, Bangalore, wherein admitted as an inpatient.
So far, the petitioner has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He has aged about 21 years.
The petitioner was a B.B.A student at Jems B School at Bangalore and also doing Electrical work as part time job and earning sum of Rs.20,000/- pm.,.
Due to the permanent disability petitioner is not in a position to concentrate on his studies.

He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability,
loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - the R.C. owner of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-NA-8989 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed Ex-parte.

5. The Respondent no.2/the insurer of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-NA-8989 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the insured vehicle was not involved in the accident, that the petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional police and the owner of the vehicle has fixed the vehicle for unlawful gain.

It is further contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding a valid driving license and that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner himself who without wearing helmet was riding the motorcycle.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.

sentences.text:
Based on the pleadings, this tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 18-04-2024 at about 1-50 pm., near BFW Junction, Pipeline road,
Yeshwanthapura, Bangalore City, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-NA- 8989?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3

. What order or Award ?
8.
The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and one witness is examined as PW.2 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P16.

On the other hand, the respondent no.2 has examined its official as RW.1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.
9.

My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;

REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 18-04-2024 at about 1-50 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding in Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LQ-0743 on Pipe line road and when he reached near B.F.W. Junction,
Yeshwanthapura, Bangalore, at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-NA-8989 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioner, result of which he fell down and sustained injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 8 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, police intimation, Mahazar,
sketch, Notice u/Sec.133, reply, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet, etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Abhinav Karun, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0046/2024 by Yeshwanthapura Traffic Police for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IMV and U/Sec.134(a & b), 187 of MV Act.

After completion of investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle Abhinav Karun vs Shashi Kumar N C on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77253231/
3 for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IMV and U/Sec.134(a & b), 187 of MV Act.
13.

sentences.text: So for as the involvement of offending vehicle and rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, though the respondent No.2 in the written statement has disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident but during the course of argument the leaned counsel for respondent No.2 has submitted that they are not disputing the accident.

14. So for as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, it is not in dispute that at the time of accident the petitioner was proceeding from outer ring road towards B.F.W junction.
The offending vehicle was proceeding from B.F.W junction towards outer ring road.

The Sketch clearly reveals that the driver of the offending vehicle by taking his vehicle on the extreme right side of the road hit to the motorcycle which was proceeding on the left side of the road.
Had the driver of the offending vehicle driven his vehicle on the left side of his road this accident would not have occurred.
Hence, the police records and the oral evidence of petitioner would suffice to prove the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of offending vehicle in causing the accident.
15. It is true that there is delay of 10 days in lodging the complaint as the accident in question has occurred on 18.04.2024 and complaint came to be lodged on 29.04.2024.
In the complaint and in the FIR reason for delay has been explained stating that petitioner was taking treatment as inpatient, hence they could not lodge the complaint in time.
If the medical records are perused, the history of RTA is mentioned as "four wheeler hit to the two wheeler".
The said document further discloses that soon after the accident the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient on the history of injury sustained in the accident.

When the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient on the history of RTA, the concerned hospital has to register in MLC and they have to give intimation to the jurisdictional P.S. and jurisdictional P.S. has to record the statement of injured.
Hence for the fault of the hospital authority and jurisdictional PS the petitioner cannot be found faulted with.

Hence,
the reason for delay has been satisfactorily explained.
Hence Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and discharge summary which are marked at Ex.P7 and Ex.P12.
On going through the medical document it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment at Ramaiah Hospital, Bangalore as an inpatient from 18-04-2024 to 20-04- 2024 for a period of 2 days.
As per the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained two injuries which are simple in nature.
17. Dr. Manjunath K N - Plastic Surgeon at M S Ramaiah Medical College Hospital, Bangalore is examined as PW.2 and through him case sheet is marked as Ex.P16.

sentences.text: PW.2 has deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of disability in OPD.

PW.2 has deposed that petitioner has not suffered any disability and petitioner can do his day to day activities without any difficulty and that all the injuries sustained by the petitioner is healed.

It is relevant to state here that, PW.2 has given evidence that at the time when petitioner has come for assessment of disability, he informed that after the accident in question he had taken treatment for the injuries sustained in some other Abhinav Karun vs Shashi Kumar N C on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77253231/
4 incident.

sentences.text: The PW.2 has deposed that petitioner has sustained simple injuries.
Since petitioner has not suffered permanent disability he is not entitled for compensation under the head loss of future income.
18. Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
19. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained two simple injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.50,000/-
towards pain and suffering.

20. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced inpatient bill for Rs.1,20,765/- as per Ex.P13, and medical bills for Rs.4,600/-, out of which as per the own evidence of PW.1 sum of Rs. 1,05,000/- was reimbursed from Medi Assist India Pvt. Ltd.
Hence it can be said that the petitioner has met medical expenses only to the tune of Rs.10,365/-.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.10,365/-
21.
It is stated that petitioner was aged about 21 years.
He was B.B.A student at Jems B School at Bangalore and also doing electrical work on part time at Bangalore and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- p.m..
The petitioner has not produced any document to prove that he was doing part time job.
But the possibility of petitioner doing part time job cannot be ruled out.
The petitioner has taken treatment for 2 days.
From the documents the petitioner has under gone surgery.
When petitioner has not produced any document to prove his income, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
The accident in question has occurred in the year 2024.
Usually when income is not proved the court will take notional income of Rs.16,500/- if the accident occurs in the year 2024.
In the present case, as per the own case of petitioner he was doing part time job.

Hence, notional income of the petitioner is taken as Rs.8,000/- p.m. and period of 2 months is taken as laid down period, thus sum of Rs.16,000/- is awarded as compensation towards the loss suffered during the laid down period.
22. It is true that due to the injuries sustained by the petitioner, it may have caused some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities, discomfort and loss of academic career to the tune of Rs.75,000/-.
23.
From the evidence of PW.1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at Ramaiah Hospital, Bangalore.
Further for 2 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.15,000/- taking into consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.

sentences.text: The petitioner has produced document as per Ex.P14 and submitted that petitioner has incurred sum of Rs.2,18,222/- towards repair charges of the vehicle.
If the averments of the petition is read in whole, petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- only with regard to the injuries sustained in the accident.
Through out the petition it is no where stated that petitioner has spend money towards the repair of vehicle which stated to have damaged in the accident.

In the petition,
the petitioner has not claimed compensation under the head expense incurred towards repair of vehicle.
Hence, only relevant issue was not framed regarding damages caused to the vehicle.
If really much damage was caused to the vehicle, it would have been repaired immediately and would have filed claim petition even for claiming compensation for the damages caused to the vehicle.

Even in the evidence in chief, except producing the Ex.P14 no evidence has been given regarding the damage caused to the vehicle of the petitioner and the expenses incurred by the petitioner for repairing the vehicle.
It is for the first time the petitioner by producing Ex.P14 has stated that he has suffered loss to the tune of Rs.2,18,222/- for the damage caused to his vehicle.
The petitioner has given documentary evidence without there being pleadings and oral evidence.
It is a settled principal of law that any amount of evidence produced by a party cannot be looked in to or considered in the absence of a corresponding plea in the pleading.
25. The learned counsel for Respondent No.2 has seriously disputed the genuineness of Ex.P14 and submitted that the petitioner has created the Ex.P14 to get higher compensation.

The learned counsel in further has brought to the notice of the court delay in vehicle being kept for service and submitted that for the damage caused to the vehicle in some other incident subsequent to the accident in question, the petitioner has got the vehicle repaired, hence Ex.P14 cannot be looked into and no compensation under the head repairing charges be awarded to the petitioner.
26.
In the light of the argument canvased by the learned counsel for Respondent No.2, if the materials placed on record is perused, the accident in question has occurred on 18.04.2024.
Vehicle was inspected on 08.05.2024.
As per Ex.P14 the vehicle was serviced on 07.08.2024.
It is after the lapse of nearly 4 months from the date of accident the vehicle was kept for repair.
The petitioner has stated that since he was taking treatment he could not keep the vehicle for repair.

But this court is not agreeing with the reason given for not repairing the vehicle immediately after the accident because petitioner got discharged on 20.04.2024 and petitioner has sustained only simple injuries and he could have keep the vehicle for repair after his being discharged from the hospital.
It is admitted by PW.1 that the entire vehicle was repaired.
If the IMV report is perused only some part of the vehicle was damaged.
But if Ex.P14 is perused every part of the vehicle was serviced.
If Ex.P14 is perused, it is a tax invoice and there is no seal regarding the amount paid by the petitioner.
The petitioner has not produced insurance policy to let the court know the IDV value of the vehicle and the model of the vehicle.
As observed supra, entire vehicle was repaired even though minor damage was caused to the vehicle.
Though the petitioner has produced bill for Rs.2,18,222/- but he has not produced the Surveyor report.
There is no evidence to say that the authorized surveyor has surveyed the vehicle and given report.

Unless and until the damaged vehicle was surveyed by the authorized surveyor immediately after the accident and survey report is given and thereby assessed the actual damage caused to the vehicle and estimated cost of repair there is no reason to accept the Ex.P14 to say that what are all the repair work done under the Ex.P14 was towards the damage caused due to the accident in question.
The petitioner has not produced the job card.

Further the petitioner has Abhinav Karun vs Shashi Kumar N C on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77253231/
6 not examined the author of Ex.P14.

sentences.text: At the cost of repetition, PW.2 the medical officer has clearly deposed that at the time when petitioner has come for assessment of disability he informed the PW.2 that after the accident petitioner sustained injuries due to some other reason for which he has taken treatment.
Hence, the possibility of the vehicle of the petitioner got damaged due to some other incident subsequent to the accident cannot be ruled out for the reason of delay in getting the vehicle repaired.

27. Hence, considering the fact that there is no pleading and oral evidence regarding the damage caused to the vehicle as the impact of the accident and the expenses incurred by the petitioner for repairing the said vehicle and for the reason that petitioner has not placed relevant documents to prove that Ex.P14 is related to the expenses incurred for repairing the vehicle for the damage caused due to the accident, under such circumstances there is no reason to accept the Ex.P14 to say that petitioner has incurred sum of Rs.2,18,222/- towards repairing charges.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head repairing charges.

Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
Sl.N Heads o.
Amount
1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/-

2. Medical expenses Rs. 10,365/-
3. Loss of income during laid up period Rs. 16,000/-
4. Loss of amenities, discomfort and Rs. 75,000/-
loss of academic career 5.

Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 15,000/-
charges and nourishing food
Total Rs. Rs.1,66,365/-

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,66,365/- (Rupees One Lakh Sixty Six Thousand Three Hundred Sixty Five only).
28.
As regarding liability is concerned, respondent no.1 is the RC owner and respondent no.2 is the Insurer of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered.

ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
